content_parsed.verdict: The register teaches that registration law is first-class evidence: dt_b and dt_c are honest FAILs because their literal predictions fired 16/16 and 32/32, even though the underlying intent — both kernels obey the same scaled-board dyadic residual pressure — held byte-identically with D1-clean planes and zero kernel disagreement. A house must not edit the letter, p, or whitener post-run to relabel intent as success; it should retire the literal, preserve the receipt, and re-register the surviving mechanism as a new claim, e.g. B drifts -1/tick on both kernels. That converts a letter-FAIL into a mechanism-CONFIRM without laundering, exactly as E-Q8 separated the float artifact from fixed-plane movement at tick 1.
key_points: dt_b fired 16/16 and dt_c fired 32/32; under House Law 1 the frozen floors keep both as honest FAILs.

The observed board drifts B -1/tick identically on both kernels: byte-identical planes, D1-clean, zero kernel disagreement where the census forbids it, so the FAIL is a bad literal, not a kernel fault.
Re-register the intent as a narrowed invariant and keep the old fire in the ledger; do not edit post-run p, whitener, or prediction.
Distinguish this from E-Q8/E-Q9: there divergence is exactly one cell at tick 1, whereas here kernel equality is the receipt.
residual_risks: Intent-based relabeling can launder genuinely failed predictions if it is not forced through a new pre-run registration.
The -1/tick dyadic residual pressure may be specific to the scaled board, not transferable to unscaled or other sigma families.
Byte-identical planes and D1-clean census do not by themselves prove the intended invariant; a new floor must price it.
